tags.gist: Wants human oversight of agentic devices required as a verifiable, tamper-evident record that a present human authorized each consequential action.
Says evaluation should demand proof that the specific act was authorized, not identity at login, without biometrics and resistant to spoofing.
Wants agentic devices distinguished by how reversible and consequential their autonomous actions are, with authorization evidence scaled accordingly.
Wants premarket proof that the device generates a tamper-evident record of authorization for every class of consequential action.
Wants postmarket retention and auditability of authorization evidence, proportionate to consequence, so surveillance is not guesswork.
Proposes positive human control for the gravest irreversible actions: no completion without verifiable authorization, failing safe without it.
Commends the agentic question and answers that oversight must be provable through a record of contemporaneous human authorization per action.
Recommends the risk framework separate agents by how reversible and consequential their autonomous actions are, scaling acceptance criteria.
Recommends premarket submissions show a tamper-evident record of who authorized each consequential action, without storing biometrics.
Says authorization records would make adverse-event investigation and fleet pattern detection tractable; wants their retention and auditability expected.
Draws on other high-consequence fields: unforgeable authorization, sometimes by more than one person, as a demonstrable operational control.
Concludes that requiring a verifiable authorization record, proportionate to consequence, makes oversight testable premarket and real postmarket.
